title: Monitored free fermions under periodic driving
authors: Aditi Chakrabarty, Alexander D. Mirlin, Igor Poboiko
abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically a one-dimensional periodically driven free-fermionic system subjected to monitoring of the local particle density. Based on the analytical approach that describes the long-wavelength physics of the time-dependent Hamiltonian in the field-theoretical language using the nonlinear sigma-model (NLSM), we reveal that driving does not alter the universality class of the problem. As a consequence, the system retains the area-law behavior in the thermodynamic limit, with an intermediate diffusive regime giving rise to logarithmic growth of entanglement entropy for a small monitoring rate. At the same time, driving leads to a renormalization of the bare coupling constant of the NLSM, which controls the space-time ``conductivity'' in the diffusive regime. We derive the analytic form of this renormalization, which becomes particularly strong in the case of a ``maximally symmetric'' drive and sufficiently short driving period. In addition, we employ the Wiener-Hopf method to investigate the ballistic-diffusive crossover. These analytical predictions are corroborated by numerical simulations of the von-Neumann entanglement entropy and the density correlation function. Our numerical results clearly demonstrate that, with an increase in the system size, there are successive crossovers from ballistic to diffusive behavior and ultimately to localization. Furthermore, in the diffusive regime, we observe weak-localization corrections that are in agreement with the analytical predictions of the NLSM. Overall, our results provide a unified analytical and numerical framework for understanding the effects of monitoring in time-modulated fermionic systems, paving a way for broader investigations of driven quantum matter.
summary: This work analytically and numerically studies free fermions subjected to both periodic driving and continuous local monitoring. Using the nonlinear sigma-model, the authors show that the system's fundamental universality class is preserved, while predicting characteristic crossovers between ballistic, diffusive, and localized regimes. This provides a comprehensive theoretical understanding of measurement effects in driven quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates how continuous monitoring of local particle density affects the dynamics of a one-dimensional periodically driven free-fermionic system.
main_result: The driving does not change the universality class, and the system exhibits successive crossovers from ballistic to diffusive behavior, with weak-localization corrections observed in the diffusive regime.
method: The analysis employs a combination of analytical field-theoretical techniques, specifically the nonlinear sigma-model (NLSM) for long-wavelength physics, and numerical simulations using the stochastic Schrödinger equation.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D chain of free spinless fermions governed by a time-periodic hopping Hamiltonian, whose evolution is non-unitary due to continuous quantum measurements of local particle densities.
key_observables: Von-Neumann entanglement entropy, density correlation function, and the renormalization of the NLSM coupling constant.
important_parameters: Monitoring rate ($\gamma$), system size ($\ell$), and the bare coupling constant ($g_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the long-wavelength approximation using the NLSM and models the measurement process via the quantum state diffusion protocol.
figures_summary: The notes indicate numerical simulations demonstrate successive crossovers from ballistic to diffusive behavior, and ultimately to localization as system size increases.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the non-unitary evolution, then applying the NLSM to describe long-wavelength physics, deriving renormalization group flow equations, and finally corroborating these analytical predictions with numerical simulations of entanglement entropy and correlation functions.
why_interesting: It provides a unified framework for understanding how measurement back-action and time-periodic driving interact in fermionic systems, touching upon concepts relevant to open quantum systems and non-equilibrium dynamics.
